newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies drift from highs into close.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies drift from highs into close.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly higher but below early highs as activity dwindled in the afternoon, floor traders said.

Mark futures staged an early runup on comments from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, who said the dollar had concluded its upward correction versus the mark and that it was important the mark remain strong entering European monetary union.
Tietmeyer's remarks followed dollar/mark's overnight rise to a new 41-month high of 1.7665.
September mark futures edged to another contract low of $0.5686 overnight, then rebounded strongly as the dollar dived.
Mark and Swiss franc futures rallied further in pit trade after the release of U.S. weekly initial jobless claims, with the September Swiss contract pushing up to a two-week high of $0.6969.
The Labor Department said claims rose to 377,000 in the week ended July 5, a gain of 40,000 from the previous week, spurred by retooling in the automobile industry.

Currency traders said the sharp rise in claims for unemployment insurance weighed on the dollar because it supported the arguement that the Fed would not need to raise short-term interest rates in August.
Rising interest rates make U.S. assets more attractive to investors, boosting demand for dollars.
Yen futures ended lower but were confined to their recent range, meandering now that the market has the Japanese trade data released earlier this week behind it, floor analysts said.

British pound futures also drifted through the day after rallying early in the wake of the Bank of England's 25 basis point interest rate hike to 6.75 percent, the third British rate increase in three months and a move that was widely anticipated.

U.S. producer price index data for June will be released Friday morning. Economists predict the index will be unchanged from the previous month, with core PPI excluding food and energy prices rising 0.1 percent.

September yen futures ended down $0.000031 at $0.008922, marks up $0.0026 at $0.5734, Swiss francs up $0.0035 at $0.6951, sterling up $0.0028 at $1.6848, Canadian dollars up $0.0006 at $0.7312, Australian dollars down $0.0024 at $0.7429 and Mexican pesos up $0.00525 at $0.124050.
